title: The weekly schedule refresh
author: Neal Mitchell
excerpt: A weekly pull-in meeting only works if it leaves behind an artifact the team can act on. The schedule refresh is that artifact — a record of where the program stands, what moved this week, who is doing what next, and what could derail it.

title: The critical path you're not watching
author: Neal Mitchell
excerpt: Most program teams focus on CP1 and miss the near-critical paths behind it. This briefing uses a real critical-path snapshot to show how buffer-burn rate flags which path becomes the next constraint, and why CP2 through CP5 all need to be shortened in step.

title: It’s the second or third critical path that can sneak up and bite you…
author: Neal Mitchell
excerpt: Focusing solely on the main critical path can lead to project delays, as other paths may slip unnoticed. Analyzing and managing multiple critical paths, especially the second and third ones, is crucial for achieving on-time project completion. Regularly monitoring and addressing potential issues in these paths can prevent delays and ensure timely project delivery.
